candidates.claim: The new lemma is named `isMulCommutative_mono`, but its statement is the *antitone* direction of the predicate `fun s => IsMulCommutative ↥s`: from `h : s ≤ t` (smaller subobject) and `[IsMulCommutative t]` (bigger subobject) it concludes `IsMulCommutative s`, i.e. the property is inherited by the smaller object. A `_mono` suffix in this library means `Monotone`/ascending (e.g. `not_isVanishingOn_mono ⦃s₁ s₂⦄ (hs : s₁ ⊆ s₂) (hf : ¬ IsVanishingOn f s₁) : ¬ IsVanishingOn f s₂`, `diam_mono`), while the descending/predicate-inherited direction is spelled `_anti` (`nth_mem_anti {a b} (hab : a ≤ b) (h : p (nth p b)) : p (nth p a)`, `deleteEdges_anti`, `generateFrom_anti`, `one_anti`). The name therefore says the opposite of what the lemma proves, and it contradicts the docstring written for it ("passes to smaller subobjects") as well as the PR title, which calls this declaration `isMulCommutative_anti`.
candidates.requested_change: Rename `isMulCommutative_mono` to `isMulCommutative_anti` (the `to_additive` companion then becomes `isAddCommutative_anti`); the statement, proof and docstrings can stay exactly as they are. I verified this rename compiles in place (whole file recompiled, no errors).
candidates.suggested_fix: Rename `isMulCommutative_mono` to `isMulCommutative_anti` (the `to_additive` companion then becomes `isAddCommutative_anti`); the statement, proof and docstrings can stay exactly as they are. I verified this rename compiles in place (whole file recompiled, no errors).
